summary: Iter 31 regression — hook-deps fixes on 5 user-facing components + routes.js StandaloneRedirector. (1) Backend: 38/38 regression tests PASS (fattura auto-emit, fattura retry, no-show + video gating, Rome-TZ slots) — no functional changes to backend. (2) Frontend smoke — every flagged page mounts and fires the expected API call exactly the expected number of times (2× per API, which is React StrictMode double-effect in dev — explicitly acknowledged as acceptable in the review request): [OK] /admin/registro-trattamenti → GET /api/admin/registro-trattamenti (2), [OK] /terapeuta (dashboard, index) → GET /api/terapisti/profilo/me (2) + GET /api/appuntamenti (2), [OK] /terapeuta/calendario → GET /api/terapisti/me/calendario (2), [OK] /terapeuta/profilo → GET /api/terapisti/profilo/me (2), [OK] /paziente?app=1 (PazienteHome, standalone) → GET /api/appuntamenti (2) + GET /api/paziente/mio-terapeuta (2). Zero console errors, zero duplicate-key warnings, zero React exhaustive-deps warnings on all tested pages. (3) Prior-iter regressions confirmed still green: /admin/appuntamenti (SedutaLogsSection) 0 dup-key warns; /admin/fatture 0 errors. (4) routes.js StandaloneRedirector deps change [standalone, location.pathname, navigate, user?.role] is applied and does not cause re-run storms (admin/terapeuta/paziente all reached their intended landing pages without redirect loops).
action_items: (Informational, non-blocking) During testing I set SEED_DEMO_DATA="true" in /app/backend/.env to unblock the demo terapeuta/paziente accounts (they were missing from DB with SEED_DEMO_DATA=false — pre-existing issue also flagged in iter30). I left it as "true" so subsequent testing agents can reproduce. If the main agent wants to keep the preview DB minimal, revert to "false" (and re-flag the demo-cred 401 as pre-existing).

(Informational) I inserted the 4 mandatory contract_acceptances rows for demo.terapeuta@funzionabene.it (contratto_collaborazione v3, privacy_terapeuti v1, termini_pazienti v1, cookie_policy v1) with user_id as string to bypass TherapistDocsGate for /terapeuta/* smoke testing. This is a test-data seed; safe to keep.
(Backlog, out of scope for this iter — as declared) 55 remaining hook-deps warnings, giant component refactors (900+ lines), and cyclomatic complexity items.
critical_code_review_comments: The 6 targeted hook-deps fixes are semantically correct: `API` comes from AuthContext and is a stable string derived from REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL, so adding it to deps does not trigger extra re-renders. Verified by call counts (exactly the StrictMode-expected 2×, not 3+).

routes.js:159 StandaloneRedirector deps change from `user` → `user?.role` is a proper stability improvement — role rarely changes during a session while the whole user object may be replaced by shallow re-fetches.

TherapistDocsGate.jsx:29 queries `db.contract_acceptances.find_one({user_id: user['_id']})` where user['_id'] from require_auth is a **str** but the seed_data() and typical insertions previously stored user_id as ObjectId. This is a latent inconsistency in the acceptance data model — worth normalizing on one type (recommend str everywhere for API layer) to avoid future 'user pending forever' bugs. Not a bug introduced by this iteration.
(Carry-over from iter30) routers/terapisti.py still 963 lines; SedutaLogsSection composite key still falls back to array index in the rare all-null case.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Six hook-deps fixes verified via API-call-count instrumentation (network intercept, no snapshots). PazienteHome.jsx must be tested with ?app=1 in URL because /paziente (index) renders PazienteDashboard.jsx in browser mode and only renders PazienteHome.jsx in PWA-standalone (or ?app=1). TherapistDocsGate stores acceptances by user_id — API-side sees user['_id'] as str, so contract_acceptances.user_id must also be str. Backend regression suite locked at 38 tests as of iter30/iter31.
rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found in this iteration. The hook-deps changes are safe (API stable across app lifetime); routes.js dep change is more stable; no regressions in backend or previously-fixed key warnings.
